rationale: Round 1 failed with a compiler internal error on extreme weights, so this candidate flattens all weights into a conservative 0.35-0.65 band with no value at either extreme, which the harness hint indicates improves internal pass-pipeline stability. All seven passes remain enabled so per-function feature-driven selection can still differentiate, but none is pushed aggressively. The workload is a small numeric kernel (Cholesky, division, power in hot loops), so RuntimeCost weights sit slightly below the other dimensions to bias selection away from transformations that would bloat inner-loop execution, while SecurityGain and DiversityGain stay at the top of the band (~0.55-0.6) to keep meaningful obfuscation pressure. SUB and FLA get the highest SecurityGain since arithmetic and control-flow restructuring give the best resistance-per-cost on this code shape. SizeCost values around 0.5 tolerate the modest text growth of a 5 KB binary, and CorrectnessRisk weights near 0.6-0.65 favor passes with well-tested, semantics-preserving implementations, prioritizing a clean build this round over peak obfuscation.
